stage-000.lore-connecting: Establishing a secure connection to central endpoint. Please wait a few seconds...<pause sec='4'/>
stage-000.lore-endpoint: Endpoint reached, sharing encryption keys... <pause sec='3'/>Done.
stage-001.greeting-new: Welcome! Choose a 4-digit PIN to secure your connection
stage-001.greeting-returning: Welcome back! Re-enter your PIN to decrypt the communication
stage-001.trigram-prompt: Please, enter your Agent Trigram <red>(always reuse the same 3 letters if you have been disconnected)</red>: <input var='Trigram'/><pause sec='2'/>
stage-002.line-01:
Thank you! Now, please wait for agent contact...
<pause sec='5'/>
stage-003.line-02: Hi there! I am Tank, your Operator and I am here to help you.
stage-003.line-03: Please tell me your agent name <red>(limit yourself to a maximum of 24 characters)</red>: <input var='Username'/><pause sec='4'/>
stage-003.line-04: Hi agent <white>{Username}</white>, it's our first time together. Don't be afraid, you are in good hands!<pause sec='2'/>
stage-003.line-05: We do not have too much time, I will guide you during this mission. Please follow my instructions closely.<pause sec='5'/>
stage-004.line-02: <white>{Username}</white>, we have intercepted a message from the vilains and we now have access to their Nutanix cluster.
stage-004.line-03: They don't care about elementary security rules, it is our chance.
stage-006.line-05: We need to act quickly! You are used to this kind of situation... <pause sec='3'/>
stage-006.line-06: First we have to create a new local administrator for this Cluster, in case the vilains change the password. They are sharing passwords using emails, but they probably have a change policy.
stage-006.line-07: Please, connect to the cluster and create a new user <white>{Trigram}-adm</white>. This can be done in the <white>Admin Center</white> part of the GUI.
stage-006.line-08:
<red>Be careful when you login, the </red><white>{PCUser}</white><red> user is a local account!</red>
<image src='stage-006-local-account.png' alt='Nutanix login screen — click the Local Account link to switch.'/>
stage-007.line-01: Now create an <white>Authorization Policy</white> named <white>{Trigram}-auth</white> to give <white>Super Admin</white> rights to <white>{Trigram}-adm</white>.
stage-008.line-02: Now, disconnect from Nutanix Prism Central and connect back with your new user <white>{Trigram}-adm</white>. Hit <white>Enter</white> when you are in.<input/>
stage-009.line-01: I don't have time to check if you are really connected with the account <white>{Trigram}-adm</white>! I trust you this time <white>{Username}</white>, even if the error is (only) human...<pause sec='2'/>
stage-009.line-02: I need you to create a new project. Projects are used to group resources, manage access rights and define quotas. It is the Nutanix way to handle tenants. Users from other projects won't see what we do in our own project.
stage-009.line-03: <red>Oh... Just one important thing!</red> If I forgot to guide you into the right part of the interface, use the <white>search bar</white> at the top of Prism Central UI! It is soooo useful to move quickly from one page to another.<pause sec='3'/>
stage-009.line-04: Let's try it! Type <white>projects</white> in the search bar, then create a new project named <white>{Trigram}-proj</white> with user <white>TheProjectManager</white> as <white>Project Admin</white>.
stage-009.line-05: Finally, after having created the project, go in the <white>Infrastructure</white> tab of this project, add a new infrastructure with our Nutanix cluster and the VLAN named <white>secondary</white>.
stage-009.line-06: Press <white>Enter</white> when the project is created. <input/>
stage-010.line-02: You know what?<pause sec='1'/> I already feel that we are great teammates!<pause sec='3'/>
stage-010.line-03: Bob has updated switch configuration. You need to create a new subnet in the Nutanix cluster to use it. It should help us to extract data outside without being detected.
stage-010.line-04: Go in the <white>Infrastructure</white> menu and create a new subnet named <white>{Trigram}-subnet</white> with the VLAN ID <white>{Vlanid}</white>.
stage-010.line-05: Subnet can provide IP to VM like a DHCP and that's very useful for us. This is called <white>Nutanix IPAM</white> and please ensure to use it!
stage-010.line-06: Please configure your subnet with these informations:
stage-010.line-12: <red>Important:</red> Uncheck <white>VLAN Basic Networking</white> in the <white>Advanced Configuration</white>.
stage-010.line-13: I am waiting for your feedback. Press <white>Enter</white> when the subnet is setup: <input/>
stage-011.line-02: We are good, especially you.<pause sec='4'/>
stage-011.line-03: Before creating a VM, we need to add an image in the library. I pushed a home-made image on the ubuntu official repository. It should be enough to fake the others.
stage-011.line-04: Add a disk image named <white>{Trigram}-ubuntu</white> in the image library from this <white>URL</white>:
stage-011.line-06: <red>Warning:</red> Please ensure the image is a <white>disk</white> image, <red>not</red> an <white>ISO</white> image.
stage-011.line-07: Press <white>Enter</white> when the image is available on the cluster: <input/>
stage-012.line-02: We are on time and that is good, but we need to hurry up. I have detected an activity from the others... they are looking for us. We need to work carefully.
stage-012.line-03: Please, create a new VM named <white>{Trigram}-vm</white> with the following configuration:
stage-012.line-06: - <white>20GB</white> disk based on image we just uploaded
stage-012.line-09:
You can use this <white>cloud-init</white> to create a few users in this VM:
<pause sec='1'/>
stage-012.line-10: #cloud-config users: - name: nutanix shell: /bin/bash sudo: ['ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL'] - name: admin shell: /bin/bash sudo: ['ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL'] primary_group: users groups: [sudo] no_user_group: true chpasswd: list: | nutanix:MyPassword admin:MyPassword expire: false ssh_pwauth: true
stage-012.line-11: After that, move your VM into your project with <white>Manage Ownership</white> action in the VM contextual menu.
stage-012.line-12: When it is done, start the VM, and press <white>Enter</white> when you have finished: <input/>
stage-013.line-02: I am not very peaceful, there are many strange things happening around us.<pause sec='5'/>
stage-013.line-03: Please, disconnect from Nutanix Prism Central and connect back with the <red>Active Directory</red> user <white>{ProdUsername}</white> using password <white>{ProdPassword}</white> ...
stage-013.line-04: Then look at the VM list in the UI, and confirm the VM you have created is not listed.
stage-014.line-02: Perfect, it is pretty discrete. The user <white>{ProdUsername}</white> owns to <white>Production</white> project only. He is not able to see assets from others projects. So, they won't see your VM, except if they look for it. We need to be careful.
stage-014.line-03: Please, connect back with our admin user <white>{Trigram}-adm</white> on Nutanix Prism Central and hit <white>Enter</white> when you are ready.<input/>
stage-014.line-04: <pause sec='6'/>Oh wait!!!<pause sec='2'/> They are scanning the server hosting our VM. Whoopsie-daisy!
stage-014.line-05: Move our VM to another one right now! <red>I recommend you to first click on the VM and check the node it is running on and then migrate it to another node.</red>
stage-015.line-02: Thanks god, they have not detected the VM... Wooow, it was very hot!
stage-015.line-03: Now we are starting serious things. Unfortunately, you are not Nutanix certified, but it is not a big deal. Nutanix makes things simple with their interface and you should easily find how to do things by yourself.<pause sec='4'/>
stage-015.line-04: In the <white>Admin Center</white> page, you should find something to manage categories. Nutanix uses Catagories to manage all the policies on the cluster, it is very efficient.<pause sec='3'/>
stage-015.line-05: Create a new category <white>{Trigram}-cat</white> with 2 values : <white>Critical</white> and <white>Test</white>.<pause sec='3'/>
stage-015.line-06: I am waiting for your feedback ... press <white>Enter</white> when it's done: <input/>
stage-015.line-08: Nice, you work quickly. I expect you didn't do it dirty... <pause sec='4'/>
stage-016.line-01: Can you go back in the <white>Infrastructure</white> page on your VM view and apply the category <white>{Trigram}-cat</white> with value <white>Critical</white> to it please?
stage-017.line-02: Now we are going to create different policies to protect our VM and first we are going to encrypt it!<pause sec='3'/>
stage-017.line-03: For that, you need to create a Storage policy <white>{Trigram}-sto-policy</white> enabling the encryption. You can use the default values for the other fields cause we do not really care about them here, but if you are curious, take a look at them, it is interesting.
stage-017.line-04: Apply it to VMs with your category <white>{Trigram}-cat</white> and the value <white>Critical</white>.
stage-017.line-07: Let me check this storage policy...
stage-018.line-02: Now, create a security policy to enable microsegmentation and protect our VM. <pause sec='3'/>It is a way to control network exchange between the VM and other elements of the network. It is very useful to avoid any data leak or attack.<pause sec='3'/>
stage-018.line-03: It's a bit of a shame to have this feature and not use it. It would have hampered our mission if the villains had known about it and used it... <pause sec='5'/>
stage-018.line-04: Anyway... Create a new Security policy named <white>{Trigram}-mseg-policy</white> with the following rules:
stage-018.line-06: - Policy Hitlogs: <white>Enabled</white> handy for monitoring inbound traffic
stage-018.line-07: - <white>Deny all inboud/incoming traffic</white> to the VM
stage-018.line-08: - Apply it to your category <white>{Trigram}-cat</white> with value <white>Critical</white>
stage-018.line-13: I am going to check that security policy...
stage-019.line-02: Next step, connect with ssh on <white>{Trigram}-vm</white>... As a reminder, the user and password defined in the cloud-init were <white>admin</white> and <white>MyPassword</white>. Your turn... <pause sec='5'/>
stage-019.line-03: Oh wait, it won't work with our security policy... My bad!<pause sec='2'/>
stage-019.line-04: First check if our Security policy is working as we expect, with a simple ping to your VM. It should not work. To execute your ping, open the SSH console in a new tab — it'll run a new terminal session on a VM on the Nutanix cluster.
stage-019.line-05: Then update the policy to allow the SSH and icmp traffic.
stage-019.line-06: To do that, <white>allow all inbound traffic</white> and add the 2 below <white>Traffic Filtering</white> rules:
stage-019.line-09: After Security policy update, check again the ping and press <white>Enter</white>: <input/>
stage-019.line-11: I trust you but I prefer to double-check that, buddy...
stage-020.line-02: We have a last policy to setup: a protection policy. It is a way to pilot snapshots and their replication, to reduce disaster impact.<pause sec='5'/>
stage-020.line-03: Create a new Protection policy named <white>{Trigram}-prot-policy</white> with the following properties:
stage-020.line-04: - No need to replicate, so <white>no need for a Recovery Location</white>
stage-020.line-05: - Just a <white>local schedule</white>, with the below settings:
stage-020.line-09: - Applied to VM with your categorie <white>{Trigram}-cat</white> and value <white>Critical</white>.<pause sec='2'/>
stage-020.line-12: Good. I check again. Less risks, more fun!
stage-021.line-01: To secure our work, we are going to setup an approval policy for snapshot deletion. It will avoid any deletion of our snapshots by our... embarrassing friends!
stage-021.line-02: For that, we must create an approval policy with the below settings:<pause sec='3'/>
stage-021.line-05: - 3 approvers in this set : <white>Charlie</white>, <white>Thom</white> and <white>William</white> <red>(add them with lowercase names)</red>.
stage-021.line-07: <red>Warning: this policy may already exist and only one approval policy is allowed. In this case, simply link it to your protection policy as described below.</red>.<pause sec='2'/>
stage-021.line-08: Then associate your protection policy <white>{Trigram}-prot-policy</white> to the existing or created approval policy.<pause sec='4'/>
stage-021.line-11: Nice. I'll check this... give me two seconds please...<pause sec='2'/>
stage-022.line-01: To be sure the recovery points are protected, just look back at the protection policy page, and ensure your policy has a <white>Secure</white> mention.<pause sec='2'/>
stage-023.line-02: Oh oh... <pause sec='3'/>Don't move please!<pause sec='5'/><action name='deleteVM'/>
stage-023.line-03: Seems that they are inspecting the cluster... Do not do anything. I'm closing the connection to reconnect with a more securized protocol. Wait here, please!
stage-024.line-05: Establishing connection to the endpoint with multi-layer encryption and multiple hops to reduce tracking capabilities...<pause sec='3'/> Connected successfully!
stage-025.line-01: Ok, I'm back. I hope you are still there and in good shape, buddy!
stage-025.line-03: We make a great team <white>{Username}</white>!<pause sec='3'/> We have a job to finish, let's get back to it!<pause sec='5'/>
stage-026.line-03: I can't believe it... but it looks like they have deleted our VM! Fortunately, we still have available recovery points.<pause sec='3'/>
stage-026.line-04: <red>Clone</red> the VM from the latest recovery point available, using its original name <white>{Trigram}-vm</white> as before! Then start it.
stage-026.line-05: I will update myself in the meantime. Note that the <white>Clone</white> operation is no more that a <red>restore</red> process of the VM!
stage-027.line-02: You know what? Since we have a bit of time, let's spy on them. <pause sec='2'/>
stage-027.line-03: Send to this discreet address <white>{Trigram}{EmailReport}</white> a report with the <white>list of VMs</white>, <white>every day at 03:00 AM</white>. <pause sec='3'/>
stage-027.line-04: Reports are managed in the <white>Intelligent Operations</white> part of the GUI. Name it <white>{Trigram}-report</white>. <pause sec='2'/>
stage-027.line-07: Received loud and clear. I'll check this... give me two seconds please...<pause sec='2'/>
stage-028.line-02: Now I need you go on the <white>Infrastructure > Hardware > Clusters</white> page. Then simulate cluster expansion, <red>without validating it</red>!
stage-028.line-03: Just take a screenshot of the review page, it will be useful for a future mission. I can't tell you more right know. <pause sec='3'/>
stage-028.line-04: Please give me <white>the serial number</white> of the new node : <input var='NodeSerial'/>
stage-029.line-01: There is another point I would like you check for this future mission: the status of the updates.
stage-029.line-02: Look at the <white>Admin Center > LCM</white> page to check <white>Prism Central</white> updates and take a screenshot of product list and current version.
stage-029.line-03: Check also if updates are available for the platform. You'll send me it later. <pause sec='3'/>
stage-029.line-04: Tell me <white>how many updates</white> are available : <input var='NumberUpdates'/>
stage-030.line-01: Awesome!<pause sec='2'/> There is one last check to do...<pause sec='1'/>
stage-030.line-02: From the <white>Dashboard</white> page of the <white>Infrastructure</white>, you should have a tile with security concerns.
stage-030.line-03: From here, display the full security Dashboard. and dig into it. Take some screenshot which will help us for upcoming operations.
stage-030.line-04: We will have to act quickly, this tool is very helpfull to identify all security issues of the platform and they probably take care of it. <pause sec='5'/>
stage-031.line-03: We have intercepted a new account for another cluster. <pause sec='2'/>
stage-031.line-04: Not a big catch, it seems to be the account of the person who monitors clusters capacity and node procurement.<pause sec='2'/>
stage-031.line-05: Can you connect on this cluster now, check runway values and give me the number of days remaining on this cluster?<pause sec='3'/>
stage-031.line-06: Required informations to connect are below:
stage-031.line-10: You should find info in the <white>Intelligent Operations</white> page. Just send the <white>number of days</white> here when you have it <red>(only numbers, nothing else)</red>: <input var='Runway'/>
stage-032.line-01: Nutanix provides advices to optimize VM size and reduce the footprint on the cluster. They will probably use it to reduce the cost of the platform and push back the node procurement. <pause sec='3'/>
stage-032.line-02: Can you check how many resources can be saved on the cluster? <pause sec='3'/>
stage-032.line-03: If the informations we have are accurate, you have to find an <white>Optimize Resources</white> button in the left pane. Take a screenshot for later please it will help us to estimate new nodes addons date.
stage-033.line-03: Ok! <pause sec='3'/>Now go back on the first cluster please.<pause sec='3'/>
stage-033.line-04: We are going to leverage <white>Intelligent Operations Low-Code</white> capabilities from <white>NCM</white>. They also call this feature <white>X-Play</white> and it is very useful to automate tasks. <pause sec='3'/>
stage-033.line-05: Can you create a new playbook with the below settings:
stage-033.line-07: - Actions: Send an email to <white>{Trigram}{EmailReport}</white> as soon as a an event happens about a VM that is <white>Power Cycled</white>.
stage-033.line-08: - Details: In the email body, put the <white>VM ID</white> please.
stage-033.line-09: <red>And do not forget to enable it!</red>
stage-034.line-01: I think we need to do a test. Can you <white>Power Cycle</white> the VM <white>{Trigram}-vm</white> and then verify the playbook has been played? <pause sec='2'/>
stage-034.line-02: If my informations are accurates, in the playbook page, you have a <white>Plays</white> tab with the execution history.<pause sec='2'/>
stage-034.line-03: Do not hesitate to look at the details of the last execution and verify that the body of the sent email is compliant.<pause sec='2'/>
stage-035.line-03: Let's continue to trap this cluster... <pause sec='3'/>
stage-035.line-04: It seems they are using <white>Nutanix Self-Service</white> to create automation and provide applications in a marketplace for their end-users. <pause sec='2'/>
stage-035.line-05: They have a blueprint to clone some VM into a dedicated network, a.k.a. <white>a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)</white>, for testing purpose obviously. It could be interesting to execute it and I'll be quiet to investigate, not in production and far from potential trackers.
stage-035.line-06: Please go in <white>Self-Service > Blueprints</white> and open the blueprint <white>CloneProd</white>. Click on the <white>Credentials</white> button to update the password of the <white>{PCUser}</white> account which allows access to Prism Central. As a reminder, its password is: <white>{PCPassword}</white> ...
stage-035.line-07: <red>Don't forget to save the changes before continuing!</red>
stage-035.line-08: Then, launch <white>CloneProd</white> with the below settings:
stage-035.line-14: - Category for floating IP: <white>Quarantine</white> (in fact, we don't care about it cause we won't use it)
stage-035.line-17: Nice, let me check that it's ok...<pause sec='2'/>
stage-036.line-01: To have an exact copy of the production VM on a daily basis, I would like you schedule an action named <white>Refresh VM</white>.
stage-036.line-02: It can be done in the <white>Self-Service > Policies</white> page. Name it <white>{Trigram}-sched</white> please.
stage-036.line-03: For your information, your app is currently deployed in the <white>production</white> project. Do a daily task, time does not matter. <pause sec='3'/>
stage-036.line-06: Awesome! I'm checking that now...<pause sec='2'/>
stage-037.line-01: <action name='deployBlueprint'/>Its time for our last task. <pause sec='2'/>We are going to modifiy one of their blueprint, to add a backdoor in the VM they will deploy.
stage-037.line-02: This blueprint is used by their end-users to deploy a new VM in their environment (IPAM, CMDB, DNS, Firewall, Backup, etc).<pause sec='3'/>
stage-037.line-03: Look at the blueprint <white>bp-blankvm-prd{Vlanid}</white> and edit it. Please add a task named <white>foo</white> in the <white>Create</white> action of the service <white>NewVM</white> after the existing <white>Add DNS Entry</white> task.
stage-037.line-04: In the <white>Execute</white> task, with <white>Shell</white> type, enter this:
stage-037.line-07: Save all and press <white>Enter</white> when it's done: <input/>
stage-037.line-09: Perfect! I'm checking that now...<pause sec='2'/>
stage-038.line-02: <green>And there you go, mission accomplished!</green> Thank you agent <white>{Username}</white>...
stage-038.line-03: It was so great to have you working on this mission and your help was decisive and valuable for your country. Now, you can close your session.
stage-038.line-04: Go back to the basecamp and have a beer or two! But do not forget to bring the screenshots with you.
stage-038.line-05:
Looking forward to working with you on a next mission! May the force be with you ...
<pause sec='10'/>
stage-039.line-02: All traces have been deleted!<pause sec='3'/>
sentences.ok-06: You are the best of the best!
sentences.ok-09: Seems that you did that all your life, didn't you?

sentences.ko-07: I knew you better — try again!
